items.title: UP Police mistakenly give Owaisi guard of honour meant for Supreme Court judge
items.summary: In a hilarious goof-up, the police in Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh, mistakenly accorded a guard of honour to AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi on Saturday, November 21, after confusing his convoy with that of a Supreme Court judge expected at the Circuit House. The police contingent had assembled at the government premises to receive the judge when Owaisi arrived with a convoy carrying Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) chief Chandrashekhar Aazad. As soon as the AIMIM chief arrived at the Circuit House, a group of four police personnel in ceremonial attire stood at the entrance of the building to perform the gun salute. Owaisi stopped and received it before proceeding inside. The mix-up was noticed shortly afterwards and brought to the attention of senior police officials. The judge did not arrive at the Circuit House, an officiating Reserve Inspector told The Indian Express . Owaisi later said he did not know why the salute had been given to him. He said police personnel asked him to stand for the salute and he followed their instructions. items.title: A private odyssey: Belonging, without reckoning
items.summary: Last summer, along Lake Como, close to the place where Benito Mussolini was captured and killed by the Resistance Group, I came across his framed photographs being sold publicly. Unlike Germans, many Italians have not had a sustained reckoning with their Fascist past, often deluding themselves into believing it to be an aberration. The summer spent in Italy returned to me while reading Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love . She records in vivid detail the kindness and generosity of her father Stefano Maino, who had served in the Italian army under the Fascist government. “Not for nothing was he known to his comrades as Maino il Leone – Maino the Lion – as much loved by his men as he was feared,” she writes. The daughterly love is understandable, but here’s a leader who acutely records the threats of right-wing politics in the country she adopted, but is reluctant to confront the one she was born in. The memoir is silent about any possible shadow of Mussolini’s military campaigns over Maino’s life. Saviour complex The autobiography is a genre in omission. The incident took place in April but came to light only recently. items.title: A Duck’s Tale: Arun Varghese on his quirky satire rooted in the backwaters of Kuttanad
items.summary: Ducks, wobbling about on land and water, are such a common sight in small towns of Kerala, especially in Kuttanad, that you don’t pause to take a second look when you hear their ceaseless quacking. So, when A Duck’s Tale , a Malayalam movie set to premiere at the International Film Festival of Kerala (IFFK) next month, begins with a flock of ducks swimming in the night, you don’t think much of it, beyond making a vague connection to the title. But Arun Varghese, who grew up in Kuttanad, manages to pick out a single duck from that flock and weave several stories around it, in his debut film. He has written and directed A Duck’s Tale with the production team that made the critically acclaimed Baakki Vannavar , released two years ago. Salmaanul, who played the quiet protagonist in Baakki Vannavar , turns into an expressive, frustrated young man in A Duck’s Tale , with both films putting him in the garb of an unemployed youth. “Yes, but in this case it is more because he is lazy, not trying hard, while Baakki Vannavar was more about the system,” Arun says in an interview with TNM.
